title: WHAT IF THE INTERNET WENT DARK FOR 30 DAYS?

segments.line: Every glowing screen, Wi-Fi wave, and city light flickers out in a sudden digital silence.
Phones turn to glass bricks. People step outside to a quiet night, looking up at a starry sky with zero screen glow.
Supply chains freeze. Bank terminals lock. Server racks hum in empty server rooms as the grid hits a critical load.
Emergency red lamps glow over paper maps and handwritten ledgers while vacuum-tube radio dials scan for static.
Rooftop antennas spring to life, beaming short-range peer-to-peer radio and laser links across neighboring blocks.
Engineers in rooftop labs wire up decentralized battery arrays and glowing holographic nodes for a new resilient network.
A dramatic cyan wave sweeps across the skyline as clean optical beams reconnect every tower in a global sync.
A solar-punk metropolis hums beneath an unbreakable, decentralized peer-to-peer orbital and rooftop mesh network.
